shortDescription: European benchmark front-year electricity contracts climbed further in early trading on Wednesday, tracking gas contracts at a 43-month high following U.S. and Iranian air strikes overnight.($1 = 0.8636 euros)

children: European benchmark front-year electricity contracts climbed further in early trading on Wednesday, tracking gas contracts at a 43-month high following U.S. and Iranian air strikes overnight.
The French front-year baseload rose 6.2% to €78.25 ($89.74) per megawatt-hour, its highest since December 2024, at 0845 GMT, LSEG data showed.
French forward-curve prices were higher across the board, with front-month and front-quarter contracts also rising. (0#TRFRBc)

The continued rise in gas prices, the approaching winter and low storage situation, and persistent dry weather causing low hydro levels have pushed the calendar contracts higher, EnergyScan analysts said.
"While none of these factors are new, their persistence continues to support the front end of the curve," the analysts said.

The German front-year baseload gained 2.6% to €123/MWh, LSEG data showed.
The German forward curve was similarly higher, with the coming months and quarters posting strong gains. (0#TRDEBc)
On the spot side, German and French spot power contracts fell on Wednesday as a sharp recovery in wind generation reduced residual demand.
The German day-ahead baseload contract (TRDEBD1) fell 24.1% to €126.05/MWh, while the French equivalent (TRFRBD1) was down 17.9% at €132.75/MWh, LSEG data showed.
German wind supply is expected to more than double on Wednesday, soaring 15.3 gigawatts to 27.9 GW, LSEG data showed.
Supply in France was also seen more than doubling, up 2.7 GW to 4.4 GW, the data showed.
The stronger wind makes the German balance more comfortable while the rest of the region also looks better supplied on the day, LSEG analyst Tabish Parray said.
